samples.summary: Preview task-click handler swallows clicks on other interactive preview widgets nested in a task item (notably `<summary>` foldouts) and turns them into an unintended task toggle
samples.evidence: `onTaskClick` only exempts `target.closest('a, button')` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:283) and then calls `e.preventDefault()` before toggling (preview.ts:303). The preview also renders native disclosures via the pre-existing foldout feature: `packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:110-115` emits `<details class="note-details">` / `<summary class="note-summary">`, and `detailsRule` trims the line before matching (details-plugin.ts:54), so a `<details>`/`<summary>` indented inside a task list item still parses. A click on such a `<summary>` resolves `closest('li')` to the same task `<li>`, passes every guard, gets `preventDefault()`d (so the disclosure never opens) and instead rewrites the source line — a document edit, synced to peers, from a click meant to expand a section. The same applies to any future non-a/button control the preview grows inside a list item. Fix belongs on the new exclusion list in preview.ts.

samples.summary: New mutating API methods (list toggles, indent/outdent) and `setTaskChecked` dispatch without the read-only guard the sibling new code applies, and the notes editor never sets `EditorState.readOnly`
samples.evidence: `noteCheckboxInput` explicitly refuses to write when the doc is read-only or the view is non-editable (packages/notes/src/view/checkbox-input.ts:25-30), but the five new `NoteEditorAPI` methods wired at packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:581-585 call `toggleBulletList`/`indentList`/… which dispatch unconditionally (packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:228-231, 289-299), as does `setTaskChecked` (list-commands.ts:290+). A grep for `EditorState.readOnly` across packages shows the editor only ever sets `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` (editor.ts:413) — never the read-only facet — so `view.dispatch` from these commands mutates and syncs a read-only note. Today the only host that mounts read-only (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:352) renders no notes toolbar and never takes the API via `onEditorReady`, so I could not confirm a live caller; the exposure is that the API surface, which is public from `@wafflebase/notes`, now has more unguarded mutation entry points than before. Fix belongs on the new commands (or by adding `EditorState.readOnly.of(readOnly)` in editor.ts).

samples.summary: CSS advertises every descendant of a task `<li>` as clickable, but the click handler deliberately ignores nested plain list items
samples.evidence: `.note-preview.note-tasks-interactive li.task-list-item { cursor: pointer }` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-preview.css:344) matches the whole subtree of a task item, including a nested plain `<li>` child. The handler added in the same change bails on exactly that case — `const clickedItem = target.closest('li'); if (clickedItem && clickedItem !== item) return;` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:288-290, covered by the 'leaves a plain nested item under a task to that item' test). The two halves of the change disagree: nested bullets under a task render with a pointer cursor and do nothing on click.

samples.summary: Preview-only view mode becomes editable through the new checkbox clicks, while the toolbar hides every editing affordance in that mode
samples.evidence: `const canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view";` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:252) hides the whole formatting group when the user selects 'Preview'. After this change the preview pane itself mutates the document on a checkbox/text click, because the callback is gated only on `readOnly` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:258-260) and the workspace notes route never passes `readOnly` at all (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:207-213). Preview-only mode therefore stops being a read surface; only the share route (shared-document.tsx:352) wires read-only at all.

finding.summary: Preview task-click handler swallows clicks on other interactive preview widgets nested in a task item (notably `<summary>` foldouts) and turns them into an unintended task toggle
finding.evidence: `onTaskClick` only exempts `target.closest('a, button')` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:283) and then calls `e.preventDefault()` before toggling (preview.ts:303). The preview also renders native disclosures via the pre-existing foldout feature: `packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:110-115` emits `<details class="note-details">` / `<summary class="note-summary">`, and `detailsRule` trims the line before matching (details-plugin.ts:54), so a `<details>`/`<summary>` indented inside a task list item still parses. A click on such a `<summary>` resolves `closest('li')` to the same task `<li>`, passes every guard, gets `preventDefault()`d (so the disclosure never opens) and instead rewrites the source line — a document edit, synced to peers, from a click meant to expand a section. verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `onTaskClick` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:267-305) exempts only `a, button` (line 277) and calls `e.preventDefault()` (line 303) before rewriting the source line. The pre-existing foldout feature emits native `<details class="note-details">`/`<summary class="note-summary">` (packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:108-115), and `detailsRule` trims the line after `bMarks+tShift` (lines 52-54) and is registered with `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote','list']` (line 104-106), so an indented disclosure inside a task list item is tokenized inside that `<li>`. A click on such a `<summary>` passes every guard: `closest('.task-list-item')` matches (275), it is not an a/button (277), `closest('li')` returns the SAME task `<li>` so the nested-item guard (281-282) does not fire, selection is collapsed (162-174), `data-source-line` is set (58-68) and the checkbox is enabled (53). Result: `preventDefault()` cancels the native disclosure toggle and a task line is rewritten and synced. The path is reachable in production — `editor.ts:258` supplies `onToggleTask` whenever not read-only, which is exactly the condition for attaching the listener (preview.ts:255). Nothing else guards it: notes-preview.css:241-286 only styles the disclosure, and preview.test.ts:239-326 covers only top-level disclosures. This is a cross-module breakage of code the diff does not show (details-plugin's assumption that native summary clicks work), so it is in the blast-radius lane, and the impact (unintended, peer-synced document edit plus a dead disclosure control) is blocking.

verdict.reason: The claimed missing read-only guard exists. (a) setTaskChecked is guarded at its only wiring: editor.ts:256-261 passes `onToggleTask: readOnly ? undefined : ...`, and preview.ts:255 / 318-324 attach no click handler and mark every checkbox `disabled` when that callback is absent; setTaskChecked is not exported from the package barrel (index.ts:17-39). (b) For the list commands, the guard is at the mount boundary and is intact: the only read-only notes mount, shared-document.tsx:344-353, renders no toolbar and never passes `onEditorReady`, so the NoteEditorAPI is never handed out there (compare shared-document.tsx:310 where the docs toolbar is explicitly gated on `!readOnly`); the only host that renders NotesToolbar and takes the API, notes-detail.tsx:198-213, passes no `readOnly`, which defaults to false via notes-view.tsx:124 and editor.ts:235. I found no other mount (design-sandbox, harness pages, tests all mount writable or without notes). (c) The new commands are also not a new class of entry point: every pre-existing API mutation method dispatches identically (commands.ts:130 toggleBold, :254 insertCodeBlock, :285 toggleQuote, :321 insertTable, wired at editor.ts:573-580), so no contract that other modules relied on was changed. The checkbox-input guard cited as the "sibling" is on a typing inputHandler, a genuinely different entry point that must self-guard. There is no reachable bypass, which the reviewer also conceded.
